notes: §1985:X.4.5.4 GR2: programs describing the same external record must use the same record-name and 'the records must define the same number of standard data format characters', while a complete REDEFINES of the record 'need not occur identically in other programs'. LinkageBinder.CallMakeExternal keys each EXTERNAL record's run-unit cell by its upper-folded data-name (the 2002 AS literal is refused at 85 by VisitExternalizedNamePhrase, COBOL0900), so every describer windows ExternalTable.Cell's one image whatever its subordinate layout or REDEFINES; the rule is a requirement on the source with no prescribed detection, and ExternalTable.Describe's EC-EXTERNAL-FORMAT-CONFLICT check runs only when >>TURN enables it. Probes: (a) an ODO table, (d/f) an S9(17)V9 COMP value -12345678901234567.8 and the DEPENDING ON counter shared both ways across two separately compiled programs; (b) a differently structured equal-size record and a group REDEFINES shared, AS literal, a doubled IS EXTERNAL (COBOL2423) and VALUE on EXTERNAL (COBOL0900) refused at 85; unequal sizes (outside the rule's 'must') run without diagnosis. The witness (PIC X(6) record redefined in the contained program) prints CDEF/ZZCDEF.

next.reason: 1985: 'each record-name of the associated record description entries must be the same and the records must define the same number of standard data format characters', with a complete REDEFINES allowed. §2023:13.18.22.4 GR6: 'each name that is externalized to the operating environment for the record description entries shall be the same; the VALUE clause specification, if any, ... shall be identical; and the records shall define the same number of bytes', and the complete REDEFINES only for a record 'that is not strongly typed'. By §2023:13.18.22.4 GR5 the externalized name is the data-name unless AS literal-1 is given, so with AS the record-names may differ (looser); the VALUE rule exists because 1985 X.4.5.3 SR3's VALUE ban was lifted. A conforming 1985 program means the same, but the requirement differs.
